title: Disclosure Bias in AI Reviewers
abstract: arXiv:2611.30410v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: AI models increasingly help to review papers, and many conferences and journals now require authors to state how they used AI. Does this AI-use statement change how an AI reviewer rates a paper, and could it change which papers are accepted? In a preliminary study, we varied only the AI-use statement of 150 ICLR 2027 submissions, in up to nine versions adapted from real statements: from no AI, through writing help and coding, to an AI research agent and an AI author. Six AI reviewers rated the versions: the decision model Jev and the language models Claude Haiku 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Gemini 3.1 Pro and Gemini 4 Argon. Across 23,652 reviews, we find that every reviewer rates papers lower on average when the statement says AI did all the work than under a statement of no AI use. The AI research agent statement lowers the rating significantly for Jev, Sonnet and Argon. We find no evidence of a disclosure bias for AI as

translated_abstract: AI模型越来越多地被用于审阅论文，许多会议和期刊现在要求作者声明他们如何使用AI。这种AI使用声明是否会改变AI审稿人对论文的评分，是否可能影响哪些论文被接收？在一项初步研究中，我们仅改变了150篇ICLR 2027投稿的AI使用声明，采用了最多九个改编自真实声明的版本：从没有使用AI，到写作辅助和编程辅助，再到AI研究智能体和AI作者。六位AI审稿人对这些版本进行了评分：决策模型Jev以及语言模型Claude Haiku 5.5、Claude Sonnet 5.5、Gemini 3.8 Flash、Gemini 3.1 Pro和Gemini 4 Argon。在23,652份审稿意见中，我们发现当声明中说明AI完成了全部工作时，每位审稿人给出的平均评分都低于声明未使用AI的情况。AI研究智能体的声明显著降低了Jev、Sonnet和Argon的评分。我们没有发现AI作为……的披露偏差证据（摘要不完整，此处截断）。
tldr: 研究发现AI审稿人存在披露偏差：当论文的AI使用声明表明AI完成了全部工作时，所有AI审稿人的评分平均都会降低，这可能会影响论文的录用结果。
en_tdlr: This study reveals a disclosure bias in AI reviewers: all AI reviewers rate papers lower on average when the AI-use statement indicates AI did all the work, which could affect paper acceptance decisions.
